+Prepared by the preprint-audit subagent; 2026-10-26 client date.
+
+Sources inspected
+-----------------
+OpenAI quantitative-contraction.tex, quantitative-reduction.tex, and main
+source at 42907c9e999cc00d6abe7a50bfc1023250edd1b9. The paper PDF blob is
+0503566e95bc587a4076573a45132d97531b8ba6, matching ProveIt's intake for the
+other cited OpenAI revision 7ef5c0cc5ca4b0e072b7a050fca09ab24bc6fa3a.
+Pinned source links and hashes are supplied in provenance/. This audit checks the proposed
+modification relative to the source's tensor-contraction interface, and is
+not a fresh formal verification of the entire ETH manuscript.
+
+Relevant prior work in the local ProveIt proposal set
+---------------------------------------------------
+The factorial Cauchy report supplies mode weights 1+b+2 v_2(b!), slope 3,
+without increasing the old column-tile count. The density-refinement report
+proves the Smith profile 4j-2s_2(j) for the odd-unit block
+1/(a+2i-2j), a unit. It uses this as a limitation, not a complete new routing
+of all crossing blocks through the recursive contraction. The present
+construction applies a full crossing-block decomposition, including every
+retained valuation level, and keeps the old family multiplicity. Classical
+Cauchy elimination and the special R=1 Smith profile are not novel claims.
+
+1. Exact factorization
+----------------------
+Fix 0<=i<a, R=2^i, L=2^a, J=L/2, and a retained T with v_2(T)=i. One fixed
+bit-i orientation has slot sequence
+  s_j = eR + (j mod R) + 2R floor(j/R),  0<=j<J,
+where e is 0 or 1. Both crossing row and crossing column slots belong to
+this sequence. Put K(x,y)=1/(T+x-y). No denominator vanishes, since the
+difference between two same-orientation slots has valuation either <i
+or >=i+1, whereas T has valuation i.
+
+For b>=0 define
+  P_b(x)= product_{h<b} (x-s_h)/(T+x-s_h),
+  Q_b(y)= product_{h<b} (s_h-y)/(T+s_h-y).
+Empty products are one. Direct subtraction proves
+  K(x,y) P_b(x)Q_b(y) - K(x,y)P_{b+1}(x)Q_{b+1}(y)
+    = T P_b(x)Q_b(y)/[(T+x-s_b)(T+s_b-y)].
+The residual is zero after J terms because every real row and column
+occurs among the J nodes. Hence the rank-one sum is exact, finite, and
+valid over the unramified coefficient field at all permitted interpolation
+values. It requires no analytic convergence argument.
+
+2. Uniform valuations and the exact Smith profile
+------------------------------------------------
+Write b=qR+r with 0<=r<R, and E_b=q+v_2(q!). For x=s_j, j<b, P_b(x)=0.
+For j>=b, factors with lower residue different from that of x have equal
+numerator and denominator valuations and contribute zero valuation. The
+same-residue predecessors number q or q+1; their excess valuations are
+1+v_2(k-h), for consecutive h. A falling factorial of length v is divisible
+by v!, so their sum is at least v+v_2(v!)>=E_b. The identical argument
+applies to Q_b. At the pivot j=b there are exactly q predecessors and the
+valuation is exactly E_b. These arguments use ordinary integer slot
+differences and v_2(T)=i only, so they remain valid over an unramified
+extension, without any invalid assertion about binomial polynomials on
+arbitrary extension-ring elements.
+
+Set
+  L_{xb} = [T/(T+x-s_b)] P_b(x)/2^{E_b},
+  U_{by} = [T/(T+s_b-y)] Q_b(y)/2^{E_b}.
+Both matrices are integral and triangular, with unit diagonal. The exact
+identity gives
+  T K = L diag(2^{2E_b}) U.
+Consequently the Smith invariant valuations of T K are exactly
+  2E_b = 4q-2s_2(q),  each q repeated R times.
+This is a constructive unit-triangular factorization; the Smith statement
+does not rest only on a determinant computation. It precludes a uniformly
+better ordered integral rank profile for this same full block, but is not
+a lower bound on other SAT algorithms or more general summation methods.
+
+3. The actual modes and routing
+------------------------------
+Let c(T)=C(T)/C'(0), as in the source, so v_2(c(T))>=a+1. Use source feature
+  ell_b(y)=[T/(T+s_b-y)]Q_b(y)/2^{E_b}
+and target coefficient
+  r_b(x)=2^{E_b}[c(T)/(T+x-s_b)]P_b(x).
+The source feature is integral and the target has valuation at least
+  w_q=a+1-i+2E_b=a+1-i+4q-2s_2(q).
+The source linear form sums ell_b(y)X_y over the real columns in this
+whole orientation half-packet. This is still a single source group.
+Its target rows belong to the opposite group. Thus every mode has exactly
+one source and one target, and the old child-network factorization is
+unchanged. Row factors remain affine in these modes. Packets with identical
+coordinate symbols have no crossing modes.
+
+For each q there are R values of r in each orientation, two orientations,
+and at most 3M/L packets. Therefore the multiplicity per q is at most
+  (3M/L)*2R = 6M/D,  D=L/R.
+The upper q limit is D/2-1. This is exactly the old family count, with a
+new slope-4 weight sequence instead of slope 3. Empty ports and earlier
+pivots give zero coefficients and cause no difficulty.
+
+4. Bit cost and precision
+-------------------------
+Every numerator slot difference is an ordinary integer, with known exact
+two-adic valuation. For each denominator, its valuation is determined from
+the ordinary residue T=t+2^{a+1}zeta: it is at most i and is unchanged by
+the extension term. Remove those explicit powers before inversion. In
+P_b/2^{E_b} and Q_b/2^{E_b}, the total remaining power is nonnegative by
+Section 2. Thus no division of an already reduced p-bit residue by a
+nonunit is required. The supplied p-bit zeta determines every normalized
+unit denominator to p bits, since the coefficient 2^{a+1} has more than
+enough powers of two to absorb the denominator normalization.
+
+Each product has at most L/2 factors. Its integer valuation data and
+unit inversions have polynomial bit cost in the source size and precision.
+All new data remain polynomial-sized. The old exp(O(L log s)) packet-entry
+routine remains valid (and the existing streamed finite-difference routine
+can also be retained). The coefficients are defined at creation precision;
+subsequent calls retain precisely those canonical representatives. The
+modification introduces no need to assume lifting preserves products.
+
+5. Weighted partition bound, including uniformity
+-------------------------------------------------
+For w_q=c_0+4q-2s_2(q), c_0=a+1-i>=1, the upper bound
+  sum_{q>=0} -ln(1-exp(-theta w_q))
+       <= (pi^2/24+o(1))/theta
+holds as theta tends to zero, uniformly in c_0>=1. For an upper bound one
+can replace c_0 by 1; the fixed weight sequence is 4q+O(log(q+2)). Split
+off any fixed finite prefix and compare the tail with slope 4-delta, then
+let delta tend to zero. This yields a rigorous uniform upper asymptotic.
+Finite truncation q<D/2 can only lower the count.
+
+When discussing a matching asymptotic, state additionally theta c_0->0
+and theta D->infinity. In the contraction regime theta is Theta(sqrt(u)/D),
+D>=2^{a_previous+u}, a=O(log s), and u tends uniformly to infinity, so
+both conditions hold. No matching lower bound is needed for the running
+time theorem, and a bound on all feasible tuples is not a runtime lower
+bound for the algorithm.
+
+For c<=6M/D families and precision p_t<=(6+o(1))MD/u, the optimized upper
+bound is
+  ln N <= (pi sqrt(6)+o(1)) M/sqrt(u).
+The slope-3 version has local coefficient 2pi sqrt(2). Their ratio is
+sqrt(3)/2 under matched schedules. The conclusion is an improved explicit
+upper-bound coefficient, not a smaller s/sqrt(log s) order.
+
+6. Revised schedule and numbers
+-------------------------------
+With r=256, rho=6/r=3/128, H=ceil(s/lambda), lambda=ceil(log_2 s), and
+  u_d=floor(lambda/(700*12^d)), a_d=2 sum_{j<=d}u_j,
+we have a_d<=6lambda/1925. Consequently
+  D_arr^2 Delta=O(s^{3849/3850})=o(s/lambda),
+  L D_arr=O(s^{102/1925}), 2L<=Delta eventually.
+The active-depth minimum u is a positive power of lambda, with exponent
+1-ln(12)/ln(128/3)=0.3379616482... . Inherited precision is negligible
+exactly as in the revised-schedule report. Using its explicit guard
+p_t=p+6hD+hu(a+1) gives equality p_t=(6+o(1))MD/u uniformly. If instead
+using the exact B_i guard from the precision report, write <= rather than
+equality because late retained levels can have a smaller dominant loss.
+
+Let gamma=rho sqrt(12)=0.08118988160479113 and
+  kappa=pi sqrt(4200)/ln(2)=293.7305083098111.
+The polynomial-space coefficient is
+  C4=kappa/(1-gamma)=319.6857570776865 <320.
+Under the older epsilon=1/720 schedule it would be324.2205333244.
+The existing slope-3 basis with the SAME 1/700 schedule gives369.1413158.
+The best boundary infimum for the existing optimized schedule family is
+slightly lower than that, so do not call the older374.3776 synthesis a
+global best. The new319.6858 certificate is below that existing infimum.
+
+7. Valid optional exponential-space acceleration
+------------------------------------------------
+Full padding makes the number of packets with unordered coordinate-symbol
+pair {g,h}, g!=h, exactly 2 Hpad D_arr/(r^2 L). A directed pair therefore
+has at most c_gh=6M/(r^2 D) mode families per q. Fix exact nonnegative
+weight budgets b_gh with sum<p_t. There are polynomially many such arrays
+because r is a fixed constant (the polynomial degree is very large).
+The exact-weight tuples of a pair can be ranked and decoded by polynomial
+dynamic programming. A local child contraction Z_g depends only on the
+pair indices incident to g, as is immediate from the packet definition.
+
+For any set E of directed pairs, the sum of pair rank entropies obeys
+  H_E <= (sqrt(|E|/r^2)+o(1)) K,
+where K=(pi sqrt(6)/ln 2)M/sqrt(u). At depth d its root-normalized bound
+is K_d<=(kappa+o(1))(s/sqrt(lambda)) gamma^d, in base-two units.
+The Cauchy-Schwarz proof uses sum_{E}b_gh<=p_t. The leading estimate is
+uniform over budgets: budgets that are a vanishing fraction of p_t have
+o(K) entropy by the old slope-1 bound; the others are in the uniform
+slope-4 asymptotic regime. There are only constantly many pairs.
+
+Partition the 256 groups into sizes85,85,86. A block of size k has
+  2rk-k^2-k directed incident pairs,
+  2k(r-k) directed pairs on its boundary.
+The maxima are36550 and29240. The total pairs joining distinct blocks
+are43690. Directly build each block table and then contract the triangle.
+The resulting recurrence has coefficients
+  A=sqrt(36550/65536)=0.7467989958713,
+  B=sqrt(43690/65536)=0.8164903515294.
+Since A/(1-gamma)=0.8127892596303<B, the time coefficient is
+  kappa B=239.828125984791 <240,
+and space coefficient is
+  kappa sqrt(29240/65536)=196.199445517575 <197.
+This is an explicit exponential-space algorithm, not the earlier unproved
+polynomial-space mode-network contraction hypothesis. The high-degree
+group tensors are evaluated by the old child interface and tabulated;
+the tensor-contraction theorem is never applied to them atomically.
+
+8. A stronger optional variant using cached groups and Strassen
+--------------------------------------------------------------
+First tabulate EACH Z_g as a function of all its incident pair ranks.
+There are2(r-1)=510 incident pairs, so this recursive-call cost has
+coefficient A1=sqrt(510/65536). Store these tables, then build the three
+block tables by the above enumeration, using only table lookups. Thus
+the A-block cost no longer multiplies a child-recursion cost.
+
+Combine every cross-block collection of indices into one index. The three
+block tensors are matrices with dimensions 2^H1,2^H2,2^H3.
+Division-free Strassen multiplication works over the source commutative
+ring. Rectangular blocking with block size equal to the smallest dimension
+gives cost exponent
+  H1+H2+H3-(3-omega)min(H1,H2,H3), omega=log_2(7).
+The three pair capacities are 14450,14620,14620 out of65536. Cauchy-Schwarz
+therefore bounds this exponent by (B_S+o(1))K, with
+  B_S^2=[43690-(1-(omega-2)^2)*14450]/65536,
+  B_S=0.76804094536198.
+This is a valid upper bound even without checking which entropy is smallest:
+take the maximum over the three possibilities, which assigns the reduced
+coefficient to the smallest capacity. Square padding and rectangular
+blocking change only constant factors. Strassen uses additions,
+subtractions and products, with no problematic division by two.
+
+Now max(B_S,A,A1/(1-gamma))=B_S. The time coefficient is
+  kappa B_S=225.5970572839233 <226,
+with the same space coefficient196.199445517575 <197. All dense matrices
+are already block tables or an output of one multiplication; their largest
+dimension product obeys the boundary-table bound. Depth-first Strassen
+uses only a constant multiple of the square block memory. Cached individual
+group tables are much smaller. Recursive table memory adds, and cannot
+multiply, the parent memory; the smaller child scale is absorbed.
+
+9. Scope and remaining limitations
+---------------------------------
+The source's arbitrary-density reduction still costs O(n log log n)
+effective wires and the contraction still has s/sqrt(log s) order. The
+optional cached method improves the explicit coefficient at exponential
+space cost, but does not establish O(s/log s), remove log log n from the
+dense case, or discharge the prior conditional low-degree interface.
+Numerical constants refer to the normalized tensor-network size s, not
+directly to the number of variables in an arbitrary input formula.
+
+Final review addendum
+---------------------
+The final report makes the uniform weighted-entropy argument directly with
+theta_e = theta / w_e. It includes zero and small exact-weight budgets,
+without a separate nonuniform saddle-point assumption. The exact-weight
+indexing code supplies polynomial-size count tables and rank/unrank routines.
+Sequential access to cached group tables is charged by restricted
+lexicographic enumeration: suffix rewinds are amortized by the assignments
+already traversed. Reordering matrix tables has only polynomial overhead
+per record. These details preserve the stated bit-cost and space bounds.
+
+The final independent implementation contains no Python assertion statements.
+Normal and optimized executions each passed 656,768 explicit conditions,
+including 180 rational and 180 unramified-extension factorizations, 19,116
+matrix entries in each family, and 436 exhaustive small-minor evaluations.
+These finite tests support the implementation; the all-size conclusions
+rest on the report's proofs and its explicitly imported preprint identities.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Compile report.tex with shell escape disabled; keep auxiliary files separate."""
+from pathlib import Path
+import shutil
+import subprocess
+
+root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+build = root / "_build"
+build.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+if not shutil.which("pdflatex"):
+    raise SystemExit("pdflatex is required; install a standard LaTeX distribution.")

+         "-file-line-error", "-output-directory", str(build), "report.tex"],
+        cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)
+    (build / f"pass_{iteration}.txt").write_text(result.stdout + result.stderr, encoding="utf-8")
+    if result.returncode:
+        print(result.stdout[-10000:])
+        raise SystemExit(f"LaTeX failed on pass {iteration}; see _build/pass_{iteration}.txt")
+    log = (build / "report.log").read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
+    if iteration >= 2 and "Rerun to get cross-references right" not in log:
+        break

+    raise SystemExit("The report still has unresolved references; inspect _build/report.log")

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Reproduce the certificate comparison and finite abstract partition counts.
+
+Counts below describe a weighted mode pool, not measured SAT running times.
+All tuple counts and exact-weight indexing checks use integer arithmetic.
+Floating-point values are used only to display analytic constants/logarithms.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import csv
+import itertools
+import json
+import math
+from fractions import Fraction
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from exact_weight_index import ExactWeightIndex
+from verify_mode_graph import schedule_constants
+
+
+def mode_weight(q: int, slope: int) -> int:
+    if slope == 1:
+        return q + 1
+    if slope == 2:
+        return 1 + 2 * q - q.bit_count()
+    if slope == 3:
+        return 1 + 3 * q - 2 * q.bit_count()
+    if slope == 4:
+        return 1 + 4 * q - 2 * q.bit_count()
+    raise ValueError("unknown mode basis")
+
+
+def abstract_count(precision: int, colors: int, slope: int) -> int:
+    coefficients = [0] * precision
+    coefficients[0] = 1
+    q = 0
+    while mode_weight(q, slope) < precision:
+        weight = mode_weight(q, slope)
+        for _ in range(colors):
+            for total in range(weight, precision):
+                coefficients[total] += coefficients[total - weight]
+        q += 1
+    return sum(coefficients)
+
+
+def verify_indexing() -> dict:
+    examples = [(), (1,), (2,), (1, 3), (2, 2, 6), (3, 5, 8), (1, 3, 3, 7)]
+    totals_checked = vectors_checked = 0
+    for weights in examples:
+        indexer = ExactWeightIndex(weights, 16)
+        for total in range(17):
+            expected = [t for t in itertools.product(
+                *(range(total // w + 1) for w in weights))
+                if sum(w * e for w, e in zip(weights, t)) == total]
+            actual = list(indexer.tuples(total))
+            if actual != expected or len(actual) != indexer.count(total):
+                raise ArithmeticError(("exact-weight enumeration", weights, total))
+            totals_checked += 1
+            for rank, vector in enumerate(actual):
+                if indexer.rank(vector) != (total, rank):
+                    raise ArithmeticError(("ranking", weights, vector))
+                vectors_checked += 1
+    rejected = 0
+    for weights, maximum in [((0,), 2), ((-1, 2), 4), ((1,), -1)]:
+        try:
+            ExactWeightIndex(weights, maximum)
+        except ValueError:
+            rejected += 1
+        else:
+            raise ArithmeticError("invalid indexer was accepted")
+    return {"status": "PASS", "exact_weight_totals_checked": totals_checked,
+            "rank_unrank_vectors_checked": vectors_checked,
+            "invalid_inputs_rejected": rejected}
+
+
+def family_infimum() -> dict:
+    # This is the already-described continuous boundary family. An integer
+    # group count and a strict packing margin are needed for an algorithm.
+    def derivative_equation(r):
+        return (r / 6) ** (2 / 3) - 1 - 2 * math.log(r)
+    lo, hi = 200.0, 300.0
+    for _ in range(80):
+        mid = (lo + hi) / 2
+        if derivative_equation(mid) > 0:
+            hi = mid
+        else:
+            lo = mid
+    r = (lo + hi) / 2
+    geometric = (2 * math.pi * math.sqrt(480 * math.log2(r)) /
+                 (math.log(2) * (1 - (6 / r) ** (2 / 3)) ** 1.5))
+    return {"continuous_r_approx": r,
+            "geometric_boundary_infimum_approx": geometric,
+            "existing_slope3_boundary_infimum_approx": geometric / math.sqrt(3),
+            "new_slope4_boundary_infimum_approx": geometric / 2,
+            "scope": "Numerical evaluation of a specified boundary certificate family, not an attained boundary algorithm or a runtime lower bound."}
+
+
+def exact_rounded_certificates() -> dict:
+    """Certify the convenient rounded bounds without floating-point tests.
+
+    The classical bound pi < 22/7 is the sole supplied transcendental
+    inequality; the needed bounds on ln(2), sqrt(12), and log_2(7) are
+    reduced below to positive rational series terms and integer powers.
+    """
+    ln2_lower = Fraction(6931, 10000)
+    series_lower = 2 * sum(
+        (Fraction(1, (2*j+1) * 3**(2*j+1)) for j in range(4)), Fraction())
+    if not series_lower > ln2_lower:
+        raise ArithmeticError("logarithm lower bound failed")
+    if not Fraction(12) < Fraction(52, 15)**2:
+        raise ArithmeticError("gamma upper bound failed")
+    if not 7**100 < 2**281:
+        raise ArithmeticError("Strassen exponent upper bound failed")
+    kappa_squared_upper = Fraction(22, 7)**2 * 4200 / ln2_lower**2
+    fast_squared_upper = Fraction(43690, 65536) - (
+        (1 - Fraction(81, 100)**2) * Fraction(14450, 65536))
+    bounds = {
+        "polynomial_space_time": (320, kappa_squared_upper / Fraction(147, 160)**2),
+        "cached_strassen_time": (226, kappa_squared_upper * fast_squared_upper),
+        "cached_strassen_space": (197, kappa_squared_upper * Fraction(29240, 65536)),
+    }
+    records = {}
+    for name, (limit, squared_upper) in bounds.items():
+        margin = limit**2 - squared_upper
+        if margin <= 0:
+            raise ArithmeticError(("rounded coefficient failed", name))
+        records[name] = {"coefficient_strictly_below": limit,
+                         "squared_rational_upper_bound": str(squared_upper),
+                         "squared_rational_margin": str(margin)}
+    return {"status": "PASS", "ln2_four_term_lower_bound": str(series_lower),
+            "pi_upper_bound_used": "22/7", "certificates": records}
+
+
+def main():
+    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+    out = root / "results"
+    out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+    rows = []
+    for colors in (1, 4, 16):
+        for precision in (64, 128, 256, 512):
+            counts = [abstract_count(precision, colors, slope) for slope in range(1, 5)]
+            if not all(counts[j] >= counts[j + 1] for j in range(3)):
+                raise ArithmeticError("mode-count monotonicity failed")
+            row = {"colors": colors, "precision": precision}
+            for slope, count in enumerate(counts, 1):
+                row[f"slope{slope}_count"] = str(count)
+                row[f"slope{slope}_log2_count"] = math.log2(count)
+            row["log_count_ratio_4_to_3"] = math.log2(counts[3]) / math.log2(counts[2])
+            rows.append(row)
+    with (out / "mode_count_comparison.csv").open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
+        writer = csv.DictWriter(stream, fieldnames=list(rows[0]))
+        writer.writeheader()
+        writer.writerows(rows)
+    summary = {"status": "PASS", "scope": "Analytic coefficient evaluations and exact finite abstract mode counts, not SAT benchmarks.",
+               "constants": schedule_constants(), "existing_schedule_family": family_infimum(),
+               "exact_rounded_certificates": exact_rounded_certificates(),
+               "indexing_checks": verify_indexing(), "partition_models_checked": len(rows),
+               "mode_count_rows": rows}
+    (out / "certificate_comparison.json").write_text(json.dumps(summary, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
+    print(json.dumps({"status": "PASS", "partition_models_checked": len(rows),
+                      "indexing_checks": summary["indexing_checks"],
+                      "output": str(out / "certificate_comparison.json")}, sort_keys=True))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+"""Polynomial-resource exact-weight tuple indexing used by the mode graph.
+
+The dynamic program counts nonnegative exponent vectors. It does not store
+the exponentially many vectors, and supports exact ranking and unranking.
+All weights are positive integers, as they are for the Cauchy modes.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+
+class ExactWeightIndex:
+    def __init__(self, weights: tuple[int, ...] | list[int], max_weight: int):
+        if max_weight < 0 or any(not isinstance(w, int) or w <= 0 for w in weights):
+            raise ValueError("weights must be positive integers and budget nonnegative")
+        self.weights = tuple(weights)
+        self.max_weight = max_weight
+        v = len(self.weights)
+        self.suffix = [[0] * (max_weight + 1) for _ in range(v + 1)]
+        self.suffix[v][0] = 1
+        for j in range(v - 1, -1, -1):
+            weight = self.weights[j]
+            for total in range(max_weight + 1):
+                self.suffix[j][total] = self.suffix[j + 1][total]
+                if total >= weight:
+                    self.suffix[j][total] += self.suffix[j][total - weight]
+
+    def count(self, total: int) -> int:
+        if not 0 <= total <= self.max_weight:
+            raise ValueError("total is outside the indexed range")
+        return self.suffix[0][total]
+
+    def unrank(self, total: int, index: int) -> tuple[int, ...]:
+        if not 0 <= index < self.count(total):
+            raise ValueError("index is outside the exact-weight list")
+        budget = total
+        result = []
+        for j, weight in enumerate(self.weights):
+            for exponent in range(budget // weight + 1):
+                completions = self.suffix[j + 1][budget - exponent * weight]
+                if index < completions:
+                    result.append(exponent)
+                    budget -= exponent * weight
+                    break
+                index -= completions
+            else:
+                raise ArithmeticError("inconsistent completion table")
+        if budget or index:
+            raise ArithmeticError("unranking did not consume the budget")
+        return tuple(result)
+
+    def rank(self, exponents: tuple[int, ...] | list[int]) -> tuple[int, int]:
+        if len(exponents) != len(self.weights) or any(
+                not isinstance(e, int) or e < 0 for e in exponents):
+            raise ValueError("invalid exponent vector")
+        total = sum(w * e for w, e in zip(self.weights, exponents))
+        self.count(total)
+        budget, index = total, 0
+        for j, (weight, exponent) in enumerate(zip(self.weights, exponents)):
+            for smaller in range(exponent):
+                index += self.suffix[j + 1][budget - smaller * weight]
+            budget -= exponent * weight
+        return total, index
+
+    def tuples(self, total: int):
+        for index in range(self.count(total)):
+            yield self.unrank(total, index)

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Exact joint Cauchy modes for the ETH contraction packet.
+
+This is a local algebraic prototype, not an end-to-end SAT solver.
+Only Python's standard library is required. Arithmetic is exact over Q or
+Q[U]/(U^2+U+1); no floating-point calculation is used.
+
+For R=2^i and s_j=(j mod R)+2R floor(j/R), the Cauchy identity is
+
+  C(T)/(C'(0)(T+s_j-s_k)) = sum_b target_b(j) source_b(k).
+
+Both normalized row and source factors are integral at 2. The target has
+valuation at least a+1-i+2*(q+v_2(q!)), q=floor(b/R). All divisions by powers
+of two in their construction are exact, explicit valuation cancellations.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from fractions import Fraction
+from math import inf
+from typing import Union
+
+
+def rational_v2(value: Fraction | int) -> int | float:
+    value = Fraction(value)
+    if value == 0:
+        return inf
+    numerator = abs(value.numerator)
+    denominator = value.denominator
+    return ((numerator & -numerator).bit_length() - 1
+            - ((denominator & -denominator).bit_length() - 1))
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Quadratic:
+    """a+b*U with U^2+U+1=0; reduction modulo 2 is the field F_4."""
+
+    a: Fraction = Fraction(0)
+    b: Fraction = Fraction(0)
+
+    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
+        object.__setattr__(self, "a", Fraction(self.a))
+        object.__setattr__(self, "b", Fraction(self.b))
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def coerce(other: Scalar) -> Quadratic:
+        return other if isinstance(other, Quadratic) else Quadratic(Fraction(other))
+
+    def __add__(self, other: Scalar) -> Quadratic:
+        other = self.coerce(other)
+        return Quadratic(self.a + other.a, self.b + other.b)
+
+    __radd__ = __add__
+
+    def __neg__(self) -> Quadratic:
+        return Quadratic(-self.a, -self.b)
+
+    def __sub__(self, other: Scalar) -> Quadratic:
+        return self + -self.coerce(other)
+
+    def __rsub__(self, other: Scalar) -> Quadratic:
+        return self.coerce(other) + -self
+
+    def __mul__(self, other: Scalar) -> Quadratic:
+        other = self.coerce(other)
+        return Quadratic(self.a * other.a - self.b * other.b,
+                         self.a * other.b + self.b * other.a - self.b * other.b)
+
+    __rmul__ = __mul__
+
+    def inverse(self) -> Quadratic:
+        norm = self.a * self.a - self.a * self.b + self.b * self.b
+        if norm == 0:
+            raise ZeroDivisionError("zero element of the quadratic field")
+        return Quadratic((self.a - self.b) / norm, -self.b / norm)
+
+    def __truediv__(self, other: Scalar) -> Quadratic:
+        return self * self.coerce(other).inverse()
+
+    def __rtruediv__(self, other: Scalar) -> Quadratic:
+        return self.coerce(other) * self.inverse()
+
+    def __pow__(self, exponent: int) -> Quadratic:
+        if exponent < 0:
+            return self.inverse() ** (-exponent)
+        result, base = Quadratic(1), self
+        while exponent:
+            if exponent & 1:
+                result = result * base
+            base = base * base
+            exponent //= 2
+        return result
+
+    def __bool__(self) -> bool:
+        return bool(self.a or self.b)
+
+    def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool:
+        if isinstance(other, (int, Fraction)):
+            return self.b == 0 and self.a == other
+        if isinstance(other, Quadratic):
+            return self.a == other.a and self.b == other.b
+        return NotImplemented
+
+
+Scalar = Union[int, Fraction, Quadratic]
+
+
+def v2(value: Scalar) -> int | float:
+    if isinstance(value, Quadratic):
+        return min(rational_v2(value.a), rational_v2(value.b))
+    return rational_v2(value)
+
+
+def exact_divide(numerator: Scalar, denominator: Scalar) -> Scalar:
+    if isinstance(numerator, Quadratic) or isinstance(denominator, Quadratic):
+        return Quadratic.coerce(numerator) / denominator
+    return Fraction(numerator) / Fraction(denominator)
+
+
+def power_of_two(exponent: int) -> Fraction:
+    return Fraction(1 << exponent) if exponent >= 0 else Fraction(1, 1 << -exponent)
+
+
+def factored_ratio(numerator: Scalar, denominator: Scalar) -> tuple[int, Scalar]:
+    """Return (v,unit) with numerator/denominator=2^v*unit, v>=0.
+
+    The numerator must be nonzero. Denominator powers of two are removed
+    before inversion. For integral inputs every inversion is of a 2-adic unit.
+    """
+    nv, dv = v2(numerator), v2(denominator)
+    if nv == inf or dv == inf:
+        raise ValueError("factored_ratio requires nonzero arguments")
+    nv, dv = int(nv), int(dv)
+    if nv < dv:
+        raise ValueError("ratio is not 2-integral")
+    numerator_unit = exact_divide(numerator, power_of_two(nv))
+    denominator_unit = exact_divide(denominator, power_of_two(dv))
+    unit = exact_divide(numerator_unit, denominator_unit)
+    if v2(unit) != 0:
+        raise ArithmeticError("unit normalization failed")
+    return nv - dv, unit
+
+
+def residue(value: Scalar, precision: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
+    """Reduce an integral scalar to (a,b) modulo 2^precision in F_4's lift."""
+    if precision < 1:
+        raise ValueError("precision must be positive")
+    modulus = 1 << precision
+    value = Quadratic.coerce(value)
+    result = []
+    for coordinate in (value.a, value.b):
+        if coordinate.denominator % 2 == 0:
+            raise ValueError("coordinate has a nonintegral 2-adic denominator")
+        result.append(coordinate.numerator * pow(coordinate.denominator, -1, modulus)
+                      % modulus)
+    return result[0], result[1]
+
+
+def residue_add(x: tuple[int, int], y: tuple[int, int], modulus: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
+    return ((x[0] + y[0]) % modulus, (x[1] + y[1]) % modulus)
+
+
+def residue_multiply(x: tuple[int, int], y: tuple[int, int], modulus: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
+    a, b = x
+    c, d = y
+    return ((a * c - b * d) % modulus, (a * d + b * c - b * d) % modulus)
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class JointCauchyKernel:
+    """One full crossing orientation of a padded packet.
+
+    The other orientation adds R to every row and column slot, so has the
+    identical difference kernel. Source and target groups remain distinct.
+    """
+
+    a: int
+    i: int
+    t: int
+    zeta: Scalar = Fraction(1)
+
+    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
+        if self.a < 1 or not (0 <= self.i < self.a):
+            raise ValueError("require a>=1 and 0<=i<a")
+        if not (-self.L <= self.t < self.L) or v2(self.t) != self.i:
+            raise ValueError("t must be a nonzero grid point of valuation i")
+        if v2(self.zeta) < 0:
+            raise ValueError("zeta must be integral at 2")
+        if not isinstance(self.zeta, Quadratic):
+            object.__setattr__(self, "zeta", Fraction(self.zeta))
+
+    @property
+    def L(self) -> int:
+        return 1 << self.a
+
+    @property
+    def R(self) -> int:
+        return 1 << self.i
+
+    @property
+    def size(self) -> int:
+        return self.L // 2
+
+    @property
+    def T(self) -> Scalar:
+        return self.t + (1 << (self.a + 1)) * self.zeta
+
+    def slot(self, index: int, orientation: int = 0) -> int:
+        if not 0 <= index < self.size or orientation not in (0, 1):
+            raise ValueError("invalid packet slot or orientation")
+        return index % self.R + 2 * self.R * (index // self.R) + orientation * self.R
+
+    def E(self, mode: int) -> int:
+        if not 0 <= mode < self.size:
+            raise ValueError("invalid mode")
+        q = mode // self.R
+        return 2 * q - q.bit_count()  # q+v_2(q!)
+
+    def weight(self, mode: int) -> int:
+        return self.a + 1 - self.i + 2 * self.E(mode)
+
+    def prefactor(self) -> Scalar:
+        """C(T)/(C'(0)T), with exact 2-adic cancellation in Q or Q(U)."""
+        value: Scalar = Fraction(1)
+        denominator = 1
+        for q in range(-self.L, self.L):
+            value = value * (self.T - q)
+            if q:
+                denominator *= -q
+        return exact_divide(value, denominator * self.T)
+
+    def normalized_factor(self, mode: int, index: int, side: str) -> Scalar:
+        """Return f_b(s_j)/2^E or g_b(s_j)/2^E using only unit inversions."""
+        if side not in ("row", "source"):
+            raise ValueError("side must be row or source")
+        self.E(mode)
+        x = self.slot(index)
+        if index < mode:
+            return Fraction(0)
+        pivot = self.slot(mode)
+        denominator = self.T + x - pivot if side == "row" else self.T + pivot - x
+        valuation, unit = factored_ratio(self.T, denominator)
+        for h in range(mode):
+            node = self.slot(h)
+            difference = x - node if side == "row" else node - x
+            factor_valuation, factor_unit = factored_ratio(difference, self.T + difference)
+            valuation += factor_valuation
+            unit = unit * factor_unit
+        valuation -= self.E(mode)
+        if valuation < 0:
+            raise ArithmeticError("proved factorial divisibility failed")
+        return power_of_two(valuation) * unit
+
+    def row_factor(self, mode: int, index: int) -> Scalar:
+        return self.normalized_factor(mode, index, "row")
+
+    def source_factor(self, mode: int, index: int) -> Scalar:
+        return self.normalized_factor(mode, index, "source")
+
+    def target_factor(self, mode: int, index: int) -> Scalar:
+        return self.prefactor() * power_of_two(2 * self.E(mode)) * self.row_factor(mode, index)
+
+    def entry(self, row: int, column: int) -> Scalar:
+        return exact_divide(self.prefactor() * self.T,
+                            self.T + self.slot(row) - self.slot(column))
+
+    def feature_tables(self) -> tuple[tuple[tuple[Scalar, ...], ...],
+                                      tuple[tuple[Scalar, ...], ...]]:
+        """Immutable [mode][row/column] tables with all valuations paid."""
+        prefactor = self.prefactor()
+        target = tuple(tuple(prefactor * power_of_two(2 * self.E(b)) * self.row_factor(b, j)
+                             for j in range(self.size)) for b in range(self.size))
+        source = tuple(tuple(self.source_factor(b, j) for j in range(self.size))
+                       for b in range(self.size))
+        return target, source
+
+    def reconstruct(self, row: int, column: int) -> Scalar:
+        target, source = self.feature_tables()
+        return sum((target[b][row] * source[b][column] for b in range(self.size)), Fraction(0))
+

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Generic exact contraction of a directed mode graph by three-block tables.
+
+This is a small correctness prototype for the mode-aggregation identity.
+It does not construct a SAT tensor network or implement the recursive SAT
+solver. Edge index domains and group factors are supplied explicitly.
+
+Every directed pair has its own index domain. A group factor sees precisely
+the indices of pairs incident to that group. With a strict global weight
+budget, exact per-pair weight allocations classify assignments once each.
+For each allocation, internal indices are summed into boundary tables for
+the blocks, and the remaining crossing indices are contracted literally.
+
+Arithmetic is over the integers, or modulo an optional positive modulus.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from itertools import product
+from types import MappingProxyType
+from typing import Callable, Iterator, Mapping, Sequence

+    pairs = tuple(incident_pairs)

+            raise ValueError("group received an incorrect incident-index set")

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Independent exact audit of the joint crossing-block factorization.
+
+Uses only the Python standard library. Run normally or with python -O;
+all checks use explicit exceptions and remain active in either mode.
+This is a local algebraic verifier, not a SAT solver or an end-to-end
+verification of the ETH manuscript. By default, writes a JSON record
+into the package results directory.
+"""
+import argparse
+from fractions import Fraction
+from itertools import combinations, permutations
+from math import factorial
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+CHECK_COUNT = 0
+
+def check(condition, detail):
+    global CHECK_COUNT
+    if not condition:
+        raise ArithmeticError(f'Independent Cauchy audit failed: {detail}')
+    CHECK_COUNT += 1
+
+def v2int(n):
+    if n == 0:
+        return 10 ** 9
+    n = abs(n)
+    return (n & -n).bit_length() - 1
+
+def v2rat(x):
+    return v2int(x.numerator) - v2int(x.denominator) if x else 10 ** 9
+
+def points(a, i, orientation=0):
+    R = 1 << i
+    return [orientation * R + j % R + 2 * R * (j // R) for j in range(1 << a - 1)]
+
+def exponent(b, i):
+    q = b // (1 << i)
+    return q + v2int(factorial(q))
+
+def rational_factors(a, i, T, orientation=0):
+    ss = points(a, i, orientation)
+    n = len(ss)
+    LL = [[Fraction(0) for _ in range(n)] for _ in range(n)]
+    UU = [[Fraction(0) for _ in range(n)] for _ in range(n)]
+    pp = [Fraction(1) for _ in ss]
+    qq = [Fraction(1) for _ in ss]
+    for b, pivot in enumerate(ss):
+        ee = exponent(b, i)
+        for j, x in enumerate(ss):
+            check(v2rat(pp[j]) >= ee, 'v2rat(pp[j]) >= ee')
+            check(v2rat(qq[j]) >= ee, 'v2rat(qq[j]) >= ee')
+            LL[j][b] = T * pp[j] / ((T + x - pivot) * (1 << ee))
+            UU[b][j] = T * qq[j] / ((T + pivot - x) * (1 << ee))
+            check(v2rat(LL[j][b]) >= 0, 'v2rat(LL[j][b]) >= 0')
+            check(v2rat(UU[b][j]) >= 0, 'v2rat(UU[b][j]) >= 0')
+            if j < b:
+                check(LL[j][b] == UU[b][j] == 0, 'LL[j][b] == UU[b][j] == 0')
+        check(v2rat(pp[b]) == v2rat(qq[b]) == ee, 'v2rat(pp[b]) == v2rat(qq[b]) == ee')
+        check(v2rat(LL[b][b]) == v2rat(UU[b][b]) == 0, 'v2rat(LL[b][b]) == v2rat(UU[b][b]) == 0')
+        for j, x in enumerate(ss):
+            pp[j] *= Fraction(x - pivot, 1) / (T + x - pivot)
+            qq[j] *= Fraction(pivot - x, 1) / (T + pivot - x)
+    for xj, x in enumerate(ss):
+        for yj, y in enumerate(ss):
+            found = sum((LL[xj][b] * (1 << 2 * exponent(b, i)) * UU[b][yj] for b in range(n)))
+            check(found == T / (T + x - y), (a, i, T, x, y))
+    return (ss, LL, UU)
+
+def determinant(mat):
+    n = len(mat)
+    result = Fraction(0)
+    for perm in permutations(range(n)):
+        parity = sum((perm[i] > perm[j] for i in range(n) for j in range(i + 1, n)))
+        term = Fraction((-1) ** parity)
+        for i, j in enumerate(perm):
+            term *= mat[i][j]
+        result += term
+    return result
+
+def rational_checks():
+    count = 0
+    entries = 0
+    checks = 0
+    for a in range(1, 6):
+        for i in range(a):
+            R = 1 << i
+            for sign in (-1, 1):
+                t = sign * R
+                for zeta in (Fraction(0), Fraction(1, 3), Fraction(-2, 5)):
+                    T = Fraction(t) + (1 << a + 1) * zeta
+                    check(v2rat(T) == i, 'v2rat(T) == i')
+                    for orientation in (0, 1):
+                        ss, _, _ = rational_factors(a, i, T, orientation)
+                        count += 1
+                        entries += len(ss) ** 2
+                        if len(ss) <= 4 and orientation == 0 and (zeta == Fraction(1, 3)):
+                            for rank in range(1, len(ss) + 1):
+                                expected = sum((2 * exponent(b, i) for b in range(rank)))
+                                minimum = 10 ** 9
+                                for rows in combinations(range(len(ss)), rank):
+                                    for cols in combinations(range(len(ss)), rank):
+                                        mat = [[T / (T + ss[x] - ss[y]) for y in cols] for x in rows]
+                                        value = v2rat(determinant(mat))
+                                        check(value >= expected, 'value >= expected')
+                                        minimum = min(minimum, value)
+                                        checks += 1
+                                check(minimum == expected, 'minimum == expected')
+    return {'rational_factorizations': count, 'matrix_entries': entries, 'exhaustive_minor_checks': checks}
+
+class F4Lift:
+    """(Z/2^p)[U]/(U^2+U+1), with unit inverse by the conjugate norm."""
+
+    def __init__(self, p):
+        self.mod = 1 << p
+        self.one = (1, 0)
+        self.zero = (0, 0)
+
+    def add(self, x, y):
+        return ((x[0] + y[0]) % self.mod, (x[1] + y[1]) % self.mod)
+
+    def mul(self, x, y):
+        a, b = x
+        c, d = y
+        return ((a * c - b * d) % self.mod, (a * d + b * c - b * d) % self.mod)
+
+    def scale(self, x, n):
+        return (x[0] * n % self.mod, x[1] * n % self.mod)
+
+    def inv(self, x):
+        a, b = x
+        norm = (a * a - a * b + b * b) % self.mod
+        check(norm & 1, 'norm & 1')
+        nn = pow(norm, -1, self.mod)
+        return ((a - b) * nn % self.mod, -b * nn % self.mod)
+
+    def is_unit(self, x):
+        return bool((x[0] | x[1]) & 1)
+
+def extension_factors(a, i, t, zeta, precision):
+    rr = F4Lift(precision)
+    ss = points(a, i)
+    n = len(ss)
+    alpha = 1 << a + 1
+    rawT = (t + alpha * zeta[0], alpha * zeta[1])
+    unitT = (rawT[0] // (1 << i), rawT[1] // (1 << i))
+
+    def den_unit(diff):
+        vv = v2int(t + diff)
+        check(vv <= i, 'vv <= i')
+        return (vv, ((rawT[0] + diff) // (1 << vv), rawT[1] // (1 << vv)))
+
+    def normalized_product(x, b, reverse):
+        out = rr.one
+        power = -exponent(b, i)
+        for pivot in ss[:b]:
+            diff = pivot - x if reverse else x - pivot
+            if diff == 0:
+                return rr.zero
+            vn = v2int(diff)
+            vd, ud = den_unit(diff)
+            power += vn - vd
+            out = rr.mul(out, rr.scale(rr.inv(ud), diff // (1 << vn)))
+        check(power >= 0, 'power >= 0')
+        return rr.scale(out, 1 << power)
+
+    def ratio_T(diff):
+        vd, ud = den_unit(diff)
+        check(i >= vd, 'i >= vd')
+        return rr.scale(rr.mul(unitT, rr.inv(ud)), 1 << i - vd)
+    LL = [[rr.zero for _ in ss] for _ in ss]
+    UU = [[rr.zero for _ in ss] for _ in ss]
+    for b, pivot in enumerate(ss):
+        for j, x in enumerate(ss):
+            LL[j][b] = rr.mul(ratio_T(x - pivot), normalized_product(x, b, False))
+            UU[b][j] = rr.mul(ratio_T(pivot - x), normalized_product(x, b, True))
+            if j < b:
+                check(LL[j][b] == UU[b][j] == rr.zero, 'LL[j][b] == UU[b][j] == rr.zero')
+        check(rr.is_unit(LL[b][b]) and rr.is_unit(UU[b][b]), 'rr.is_unit(LL[b][b]) and rr.is_unit(UU[b][b])')
+    for j, x in enumerate(ss):
+        for k, y in enumerate(ss):
+            out = rr.zero
+            for b in range(n):
+                term = rr.scale(rr.mul(LL[j][b], UU[b][k]), 1 << 2 * exponent(b, i))
+                out = rr.add(out, term)
+            check(out == ratio_T(x - y), (a, i, t, zeta, precision, j, k))
+    return n * n
+
+def extension_checks():
+    count = 0
+    entries = 0
+    for a in range(1, 6):
+        for i in range(a):
+            for sign in (-1, 1):
+                for zeta in ((0, 1), (1, 1), (2, 2)):
+                    for precision in (7, 19):
+                        entries += extension_factors(a, i, sign * (1 << i), zeta, precision)
+                        count += 1
+    return {'unramified_extension_factorizations': count, 'unramified_matrix_entries': entries, 'unramified_moduli_bits': [7, 19], 'unramified_polynomial': 'U^2+U+1'}
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument('--output', type=Path, default=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / 'results' / 'joint_cauchy_independent_validation.json')
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    result = {'status': 'PASS', **rational_checks(), **extension_checks(), 'checked_conditions': CHECK_COUNT, 'optimized_python': not __debug__, 'scope': 'Independent finite local algebra checks; not an end-to-end SAT solver.'}
+    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    args.output.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + '\n', encoding='utf-8')
+    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    main()

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Verify directed mode-graph aggregation and its declared schedule constants.
+
+Run: python3 code/verify_mode_graph.py
+No assertions are used. The exact finite checks compare literal summation,
+three-block summation, cached factors, and division-free Strassen contraction.
+The displayed asymptotic constants are evaluations of the report's formulas,
+not measured SAT performance and not a proof of the full SAT algorithm.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import itertools
+import json
+import math
+import platform
+from dataclasses import asdict
+from fractions import Fraction
+from pathlib import Path
+from time import perf_counter
+
+from mode_graph import (ContractionStats, PairState, blocked_sum, literal_sum,
+                        rectangular_strassen, table_factor, triangle_strassen)
+
+CHECKS: dict[str, int] = {}
+
+
+def check(condition: bool, name: str, detail: str = "") -> None:
+    if not condition:
+        raise ArithmeticError(f"{name} failed: {detail}")
+    CHECKS[name] = CHECKS.get(name, 0) + 1
+
+
+def factors_for(group_count, domains):
+    factors = []
+    for group in range(group_count):
+        incident = tuple(pair for pair in sorted(domains) if group in pair)
+
+        def evaluate(assignment, group=group, incident=incident):
+            if set(assignment) != set(incident):
+                raise ArithmeticError("factor received a nonincident or missing pair")
+            linear = sum((7 * pair[0] + 3 * pair[1] + 1) * (state.value + 1)
+                         for pair, state in assignment.items())
+            nonlinear = math.prod(state.value - group for state in assignment.values())
+            return group + 2 + linear + 2 * nonlinear
+
+        if group % 2 == 0:
+            table = {}
+            for states in itertools.product(*(domains[pair] for pair in incident)):
+                table[tuple(state.value for state in states)] = evaluate(dict(zip(incident, states)))
+            factors.append(table_factor(incident, table))
+        else:
+            factors.append(evaluate)
+    return factors
+
+
+def graph_cases():
+    for r in range(3, 7):
+        pairs = {(j, (j + 1) % r) for j in range(r)}
+        pairs.update({(1, 0), (0, r - 1)})
+        if r >= 5:
+            pairs.add((0, 2))
+        domains = {}
+        for h, pair in enumerate(sorted(pairs)):
+            # Duplicate weights with distinct values test exact-budget allocation.
+            if h == 0:
+                domains[pair] = (PairState(-1, 0), PairState(2, 0), PairState(4, 2))
+            else:
+                domains[pair] = (PairState(h % 3 - 1, 0), PairState(h + 2, 1 + h % 2))
+        yield f"asymmetric_directed_r{r}", r, domains
+    yield "missing_reverse_and_isolated_group", 4, {
+        (0, 1): (PairState(-2, 0), PairState(3, 2)),
+        (2, 1): (PairState(1, 0), PairState(4, 1))}
+    yield "no_pairs", 3, {}
+    yield "empty_pair_domain", 4, {(0, 1): (), (1, 2): (PairState(0, 0),)}
+    yield "all_pair_weights_zero", 3, {
+        (0, 1): (PairState(0, 0), PairState(1, 0)),
+        (1, 0): (PairState(2, 0), PairState(3, 0)),
+        (1, 2): (PairState(-1, 0), PairState(2, 0))}
+
+
+def partitions(r):
+    # Three nonempty blocks, including unequal sizes and noncontiguous labels.
+    first = ((0,), (1,), tuple(range(2, r)))
+    second = tuple(tuple(j for j in range(r) if j % 3 == b) for b in range(3))
+    return tuple(dict.fromkeys((first, second)))
+
+
+def verify_graphs():
+    results = []
+    for name, r, domains in graph_cases():
+        factors = factors_for(r, domains)
+        for budget in (None, 0, 1, 3):
+            for modulus in (None, 16):
+                literal_stats = ContractionStats()
+                expected = literal_sum(r, domains, factors, weight_budget=budget,
+                                       modulus=modulus, stats=literal_stats)
+                for blocks in partitions(r):
+                    for cache, method in ((False, "direct"), (True, "direct"), (True, "strassen")):
+                        stats = ContractionStats()
+                        actual = blocked_sum(r, domains, factors, blocks, weight_budget=budget,
+                                             modulus=modulus, stats=stats,
+                                             cache_groups=cache, method=method)
+                        check(actual == expected, "literal_equals_blocked",
+                              f"{name}, budget={budget}, modulus={modulus}, blocks={blocks}, method={method}")
+                        if cache:
+                            check(stats.factor_evaluations == stats.cached_group_entries,
+                                  "cached_factor_calls_only")
+                        if budget == 0 or name == "empty_pair_domain":
+                            check(actual == 0, "empty_feasible_domain")
+                        results.append({"case": name, "groups": r, "blocks": blocks,
+                                        "weight_budget": budget, "modulus": modulus,
+                                        "cache_groups": cache, "method": method,
+                                        "result": actual, "stats": asdict(stats),
+                                        "literal_assignments": literal_stats.literal_assignments})
+    return results
+
+
+def naive_multiply(A, B, modulus):
+    result = [[sum(A[i][k] * B[k][j] for k in range(len(B)))
+               for j in range(len(B[0]))] for i in range(len(A))]
+    return result if modulus is None else [[entry % modulus for entry in row] for row in result]
+
+
+def verify_rectangular_strassen():
+    results = []
+    shapes = ((1, 1, 1), (1, 3, 5), (2, 3, 5), (3, 5, 2),
+              (5, 3, 4), (4, 4, 4), (5, 5, 5), (3, 8, 7))
+    for m, k, n in shapes:
+        A = [[((i + 2) * (j + 3) + 7 * i - j) % 11 - 5 for j in range(k)] for i in range(m)]
+        B = [[((i + 3) * (j + 1) - 2 * i + 3 * j) % 13 - 6 for j in range(n)] for i in range(k)]
+        C = [[((i + 4) * (j + 2) + i - 4 * j) % 7 - 3 for j in range(m)] for i in range(n)]
+        for modulus in (None, 2, 16):
+            expected = naive_multiply(A, B, modulus)
+            actual = rectangular_strassen(A, B, modulus=modulus)
+            check(actual == expected, "rectangular_strassen_equals_naive")
+            triangle = sum(expected[i][j] * C[j][i] for i in range(m) for j in range(n))
+            if modulus is not None:
+                triangle %= modulus
+            check(triangle_strassen(A, B, C, modulus=modulus) == triangle,
+                  "strassen_triangle_equals_naive")
+            results.append({"m": m, "k": k, "n": n, "modulus": modulus,
+                            "square_block_size": 1 << (min(m, k, n).bit_length() - 1),
+                            "triangle": triangle})
+    return results
+
+
+def schedule_constants():
+    r = 256
+    blocks = (85, 85, 86)
+    incident_counts = [2 * r * b - b * b - b for b in blocks]
+    boundary_counts = [2 * b * (r - b) for b in blocks]
+    pair_counts = [2 * blocks[i] * blocks[j] for i, j in ((0, 1), (1, 2), (0, 2))]
+    crossing_count = r * r - sum(b * b for b in blocks)
+    check(max(incident_counts) == 36550, "block_incident_count")
+    check(max(boundary_counts) == 29240, "block_boundary_count")
+    check(crossing_count == 43690, "total_crossing_count")
+    check(sorted(pair_counts) == [14450, 14620, 14620], "triangle_pair_counts")
+    A2 = Fraction(max(incident_counts), r * r)
+    B2 = Fraction(crossing_count, r * r)
+    J2 = Fraction(max(boundary_counts), r * r)
+    a2 = Fraction(2 * (r - 1), r * r)
+    gamma_upper = Fraction(13, 160)
+    check(Fraction(52, 15)**2 > 12, "rational_sqrt12_upper_bound")
+    check(A2 / B2 < (1 - gamma_upper)**2, "direct_recurrence_dominated_exact")
+    epsilon = Fraction(1, 700)
+    a_schedule = 2 * epsilon / (1 - Fraction(1, 12))
+    packing_exponent = Fraction(9, 10) + 32 * a_schedule
+    check(a_schedule == Fraction(6, 1925), "cumulative_schedule_exact")
+    check(packing_exponent == Fraction(3849, 3850) < 1, "packing_slack_exact")
+    gamma = 3 * math.sqrt(12) / 128
+    A, B, J, group_a = (math.sqrt(float(x)) for x in (A2, B2, J2, a2))
+    omega = math.log2(7)
+    B_strassen_squared = (crossing_count - (1 - (omega - 2)**2) * min(pair_counts)) / (r * r)
+    B_strassen = math.sqrt(B_strassen_squared)
+    # 7^5>2^14 proves omega>14/5, hence (omega-2)^2>16/25.
+    # This yields a rational lower bound that certifies both dominances.
+    check(7**5 > 2**14, "strassen_omega_exact_lower_bound")
+    B_strassen_lower_squared = (Fraction(crossing_count)
+                               - Fraction(9, 25) * min(pair_counts)) / (r * r)
+    check(B_strassen_lower_squared == Fraction(38488, 65536),
+          "strassen_coefficient_exact_lower_bound")
+    check(B_strassen_lower_squared > A2
+          and B_strassen_lower_squared > a2 / (1 - gamma_upper)**2,
+          "strassen_recurrence_dominated_exact")
+    root4 = math.pi * math.sqrt(4200) / math.log(2)
+    root3 = math.pi * math.sqrt(5600) / math.log(2)
+    root3_old = math.pi * math.sqrt(5760) / math.log(2)
+    root1_old = math.pi * math.sqrt(17280) / math.log(2)
+    return {
+        "interpretation": "Coefficients multiplying s/sqrt(log2(s)) in declared asymptotic upper bounds; not measured running times.",
+        "r": r, "blocks": blocks, "epsilon": str(epsilon),
+        "a_schedule_over_lambda": str(a_schedule), "packing_exponent": str(packing_exponent),
+        "incident_counts": incident_counts, "boundary_counts": boundary_counts,
+        "crossing_count": crossing_count, "triangle_pair_counts": pair_counts,
+        "A_squared": str(A2), "B_squared": str(B2), "J_squared": str(J2),
+        "group_a_squared": str(a2), "A": A, "B": B, "J": J, "group_a": group_a,
+        "gamma": gamma, "omega": omega, "B_strassen_squared": B_strassen_squared,
+        "B_strassen_lower_squared": str(B_strassen_lower_squared),
+        "B_strassen": B_strassen,
+        "A_over_one_minus_gamma": A / (1 - gamma),
+        "group_a_over_one_minus_gamma": group_a / (1 - gamma),
+        "root_slope4_constant": root4,
+        "known_geometric_eps1over720_polynomial_space": root1_old / (1 - gamma),
+        "known_combination_slope3_eps1over720_polynomial_space": root3_old / (1 - gamma),
+        "retuned_slope3_polynomial_space": root3 / (1 - gamma),
+        "retuned_slope4_polynomial_space": root4 / (1 - gamma),
+        "retuned_slope4_three_block_direct_time": root4 * B,
+        "retuned_slope4_cached_strassen_time": root4 * B_strassen,
+        "retuned_three_block_space": root4 * J}
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path,
+                        default=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "results" / "mode_graph_validation.json")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    started = perf_counter()
+    graph_results = verify_graphs()
+    matrix_results = verify_rectangular_strassen()
+    constants = schedule_constants()
+    result = {"status": "PASS", "python": platform.python_version(),
+              "optimized_python": not __debug__, "elapsed_seconds": round(perf_counter() - started, 4),
+              "scope": "Exact finite mode-graph aggregation and ring multiplication checks, with separately labeled analytic constant evaluations.",
+              "checks": CHECKS, "graph_cases": graph_results,
+              "matrix_cases": matrix_results, "schedule_constants": constants}
+    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    args.output.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
